hypothesis: Retaining the small global-gradient pool while adding diverse candidates can prevent the diagnosed coverage omission. Whether grouping adds value beyond a larger global pool remains an empirical question.
implementation: Union global top-six and group-diverse top-six additions, deduplicate, fill remaining positions by global rank to twelve, return in global rank order. Three removals and at most eight accepted-search iterations, with the existing acceptance checks.

allowed_conclusion: Candidate-set containment at the same state is distinct from end-to-end search dominance. Fixing the selected case alone is insufficient to promote the method.
evaluation: Preserve every query outcome, compare diffusion union to global twelve and to nonspectral unions, record continuous and binary fidelity, actual proposal counts, and search-only timing. Do not select grouping seeds or alter configuration after examining outcomes.
cost_limit: Union and global-twelve share a thirty-six-proposal per-step cap. Global-six has an eighteen-proposal cap. Actual work can differ because trajectories and stopping times differ; equal maximum caps are not equal measured compute.
manuscript: No empirical numbers will be copied into LaTeX during this development study.
